title: Ad Tech Gets a Python Power-Up: Theaimart ADX SDK Hits PyPI
summary: Theaimart has just launched its official ADX SDK for Python on PyPI, offering a robust server-side solution for advanced advertising needs. This new toolkit empowers developers and publishers with sophisticated capabilities for website monetization, backend ad decisioning, and seamless ad operations.
content:
The bustling ecosystem of ad technology just received a significant upgrade with the official release of Theaimart ADX SDK for Python on PyPI. This new offering is poised to empower developers and publishers, streamlining some of the most complex aspects of digital advertising, all within the versatile Python environment.

Designed with server-side operations at its core, the `theaimart-adx` SDK provides a comprehensive suite of tools for everything from ad serving and tracking to sophisticated rendering. It’s a backend powerhouse, giving developers unprecedented control over ad decisioning, which is critical for optimizing revenue and user experience. This isn't just about slapping ads on a page; it's about intelligent, performance-driven ad delivery.

For publishers and website owners, this SDK is a game-changer for monetization strategies. It simplifies the often-daunting process of integrating diverse ad networks and managing ad operations with precision. The robust tooling promises to enhance efficiency, reduce manual overhead, and unlock new possibilities for customized ad experiences, moving beyond client-side limitations to offer more secure and powerful solutions. The aim is clear: to provide a robust, flexible foundation for the next generation of digital advertising, all accessible through Python.
keyTakeaways: The official Theaimart ADX SDK for Python is now available on PyPI, targeting developers and publishers.
It offers robust server-side functionalities for ad serving, tracking, rendering, and crucial backend ad decisioning.
The SDK aims to enhance website monetization, streamline publisher integrations, and improve ad-operations tooling for greater control and efficiency.
author: Staff Writer

title: Washing Machine-Sized Satellites Are a Big Deal: SWISSto12 Bags $70M for a New Space Era
summary: Swiss startup SWISSto12 has secured $70 million in funding to advance its HummingSat, a geostationary communications satellite roughly the size of an industrial washing machine. This investment underscores a growing market demand for smaller, dedicated satellite ownership, shifting away from traditional leased capacity models.
content:
Forget the behemoth, multi-ton spacecraft typically lofted into the coveted geostationary orbit, platforms that have long dictated the pace of global communications. In Renens, Switzerland, a company named SWISSto12 is quietly building a future where these vital communication nodes are, remarkably, the size of an industrial washing machine. These compact marvels, dubbed HummingSat, are not only dwarfed by their traditional counterparts but also weigh a mere fifth – about a ton – making them a genuine disruptor in the increasingly competitive space industry.

This week, the innovative Swiss firm announced a hefty $70 million funding round, a clear signal that the market is not just interested but ready for a radical shift. The brilliance of HummingSat lies in its efficiency: by dramatically shrinking the footprint of a geostationary satellite, SWISSto12 offers a more agile, cost-effective, and dedicated solution for critical communication needs. Traditionally, governments and large corporations often lease capacity on massive, shared platforms, a model that can be inflexible, prone to congestion, and less ideal for sovereign control.

SWISSto12’s significant investment round isn't merely about technological prowess; it's a bold bet on a new paradigm: the desire for outright ownership over shared infrastructure. The $70 million infusion is poised to accelerate HummingSat production, allowing the company to capitalize on a burgeoning demand for these bespoke, smaller satellites. The vision is clear: individual nations, defense organizations, or specific private entities can now deploy their own dedicated geostationary assets for vital services like television broadcasting, secure broadband internet, and critical telephone communications, gaining unprecedented control and security.

This strategic pivot in the global space economy promises to empower more players with direct, sovereign control over their orbital communications, fostering a more democratized and resilient satellite infrastructure. SWISSto12 isn't just launching satellites; it's launching a new era of accessible, dedicated geostationary services.
keyTakeaways: SWISSto12 secured $70 million in funding to scale production of its innovative HummingSat geostationary satellites.
HummingSats are remarkably compact, roughly the size of an industrial washing machine and weighing only one-fifth of traditional multi-ton geostationary spacecraft.

The substantial investment highlights a growing market preference for dedicated satellite ownership, empowering governments and entities with sovereign control over their communication infrastructure, rather than leasing capacity.
author: Space Daily Editorial Team

title: Unihertz Tank 5: The Indestructible Android Phone That Laughs at Dead Batteries
summary: The Unihertz Tank 5 is making waves as a rugged Android smartphone designed to survive the harshest environments, boasting an astounding 17,000mAh battery. Reviewed by ETA Prime, this device combines extreme durability with impressive longevity, appealing to outdoor adventurers and professionals alike.
content:
Forget fragile glass slabs and daily charging anxieties. Unihertz is once again redefining smartphone endurance with the Tank 5, a rugged Android behemoth that just got a thorough workout from tech reviewer ETA Prime. This isn't your average pocket companion; it's a device engineered from the ground up to laugh in the face of conventional smartphone limitations, promising to keep you connected when others have long given up the ghost.

At the heart of the Tank 5's formidable appeal is its truly gargantuan 17,000mAh battery. To put that in perspective, many flagship phones barely crest 4,000-5,000mAh. This colossal power pack isn't just about lasting a full day; it's about lasting *multiple* days, even with heavy usage, making it an indispensable tool for extended trips off-grid, demanding job sites, or simply for those who detest searching for a power outlet. It even offers reverse charging, turning the Tank 5 into a portable power bank for your other gadgets.

Beyond its unparalleled stamina, the Tank 5 is built like, well, a tank. It proudly carries IP66 and IP69K certifications, meaning it's not merely splash-resistant; it’s designed to withstand powerful jets of water, total dust ingress, and even high-pressure, high-temperature washdowns. This level of environmental resilience makes it an ideal partner for construction workers, extreme sports enthusiasts, or anyone whose daily grind involves conditions that would render most smartphones utterly useless.

But the Tank 5 isn't just about brawn and battery life. While rugged phones often skimp on the 'smart' part, Unihertz has managed to pack in a suite of advanced capabilities. Though specifics vary, these typically include respectable processing power for everyday tasks, a decent camera setup, and often unique features like a bright camping light or even a built-in laser rangefinder, all designed to enhance its utility in challenging scenarios. It’s a testament to engineering that you don't have to sacrifice modern functionality for ultimate durability and battery freedom.
keyTakeaways: The Unihertz Tank 5 boasts an enormous 17,000mAh battery, offering multi-day usage and reverse charging capabilities.
It features IP66 and IP69K certifications, ensuring extreme resistance to water, dust, and high temperatures, suitable for harsh environments.
Despite its rugged design, the Tank 5 includes advanced capabilities, aiming to combine durability with modern smartphone functionality.
author: Julian Horsey
